title: Pizza history: AI agent’s cardless purchase is a first for UK
summary: Papa John’s order was made without sharing bank security details – tech that could revolutionise shopping Retailers enter the unknown with AI shopping assistants on Black Friday An order of Papa John’s margherita pizzas has become the first purchase in the UK to be made using an AI agent using cardless payment technology. The order of nine mini pizzas was made as part of the Financial Conduct Authority’s (FCA) regulated sandbox trials to test the technology, using Lloyds Bank and payment specialist TrueLayer. title: Water firms to identify 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts
summary: Department for Work and Pensions to provide data about households missing out on WaterSure support scheme Water companies will use government data to identify as many as 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts, after criticism that not enough people are aware of the £428 support for their annual bills. title: Europe joins global stock market rally as AI trade rebounds - business live
summary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news It looks like it will be a strong open later in the US market – futures for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 are up 2.7% as optimism around the AI trade returns. Shares in the memory company SanDisk are up 11% in pre-market trading. Nvidia is up 4%, while Micron and Marvell Technology are both up by about 7% in pre-market. Following this revision, the annual growth carry-over for 2026 stands at only 0.1%. It is very difficult to see domestic demand rebounding strongly enough in the fourth quarter to improve this result. Business and consumer confidence both deteriorated in October and November. A weakening labour market and growing fears of unemployment will keep households cautious. At the same time, weak demand and a lack of visibility will continue to weigh on business investment. This would leave average GDP growth at just 0.1% in 2026, well below the 1.0% we expect for the eurozone. The outlook for 2027 remains very gloomy. Salaried employment fell by 94,400 jobs over the past year, a decline of 0.3%. The situation is even worse in the private sector, where 109,000 jobs were lost over the same period, a fall of 0.5%. title: UK’s taste for cow’s milk sours as sales hit record low
summary: Environmental and animal welfare concerns, and taste preferences, are behind rising popularity of vegan alternatives Has milk gotta lotta bottle? It may not have as much as it used to, with official data showing Britons are buying less cow’s milk than at any point since records began. Guardian analysis of the government’s family food survey shows the average person bought 1.8 pints (1,024ml) of cow’s milk a week in 2024-25 – the lowest level in the record’s 52-year history and less than half the amount of milk bought in 1974.
